title: The Cold-Start Safety Gap in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2606.07867v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Are tool-calling LLM agents equally safe throughout a conversation? We discover they are not: agents are most vulnerable at the very start of a session and become substantially safer after a few regular agentic tasks -- a phenomenon we term the cold-start safety gap. To study this systematically, we introduce Safety Over Depth for Agents (SODA), a benchmark that controls how many regular agentic tasks the agent completes before encountering a safety threat, supporting up to 20 preceding tasks. Evaluating 7 models from 4 families, safety improves by 9--52% as the number of preceding regular agentic tasks increases from zero to twenty. Representation analysis confirms that model hidden states gradually shift toward a safety-aligned region as more preceding tasks are present. translated_title: 大语言模型智能体中的冷启动安全差距
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2606.07867v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：工具调用的大语言模型智能体在整个对话过程中是否同样安全？我们发现并非如此：智能体在会话开始时最为脆弱，在完成一些常规智能体任务后安全性显著提升——我们将这一现象称为冷启动安全差距。为系统研究此问题，我们引入了“智能体安全深度基准”（SODA），该基准控制智能体在遇到安全威胁前完成的常规智能体任务数量，最多支持20个前置任务。评估来自4个家族的7个模型，随着前置常规任务数量从零增加到二十，安全性提升9%至52%。表征分析确认，随着更多前置任务的出现，模型隐藏状态逐渐向安全对齐区域转移。通过系统研究前置对话中最关键的部分，我们发现常规智能体任务本身是安全性提升的主要驱动力。
tldr: 本文发现大语言模型智能体在会话开始时存在“冷启动安全差距”，即初始阶段最脆弱，随前置常规任务增加安全性显著提升，并提出SODA基准系统量化这一现象。
en_tdlr: This paper discovers a "cold-start safety gap" in LLM agents, where they are most vulnerable at session start and become significantly safer with more preceding regular tasks, introducing the SODA benchmark to systematically quantify this phenomenon.
